description: System.AppDomain.GetAssemblies can take a lot of CPU time.

Under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, prefer CurrentAssemblies.GetLoadedAssemblies() (in the UnityEngine.Assemblies namespace), which accounts for assemblies loaded and unloaded by code reloading.

description: UnityEditor.AssetDatabase.FindAssets is a CPU-intensive operation and can slow down the Editor for long periods of time on large projects.

description: Camera.AddCommandBuffer() attaches a CommandBuffer to a Built-in Render Pipeline CameraEvent. These injection points do not exist in the Universal Render Pipeline, so the command buffer will silently stop executing when migrating from the Built-in Render Pipeline.
recommendation: Reimplement the effect as a ScriptableRendererFeature with a custom ScriptableRenderPass in URP, instead of injecting CommandBuffers via Camera.AddCommandBuffer().

description: The UnityEngine.Rendering.PostProcessing namespace belongs to the Post Processing Stack v2 package, which targets the Built-in Render Pipeline. URP has its own integrated post-processing system, so this code will not work when migrating from the Built-in Render Pipeline.
recommendation: Migrate Post Processing v2 effects and profiles to URP's Volume-based post-processing using the Render Pipeline Converter.

title: Camera.allowHDR
description: Setting Camera.allowHDR has no effect under the Universal Render Pipeline, where HDR is controlled by the HDR option on the URP Asset and per-camera through UniversalAdditionalCameraData. Code that toggles this property will not change rendering when migrating from the Built-in Render Pipeline.
recommendation: Control HDR via the HDR option on the URP Asset, or per-camera through camera.GetUniversalAdditionalCameraData(), instead of setting Camera.allowHDR.

title: Camera.allowMSAA
description: Setting Camera.allowMSAA has no effect under the Universal Render Pipeline, where MSAA is controlled by the Anti Aliasing (MSAA) setting on the URP Asset. Code that toggles this property will not change rendering when migrating from the Built-in Render Pipeline.
recommendation: Configure MSAA through the Anti Aliasing (MSAA) setting on the URP Asset instead of setting Camera.allowMSAA.

title: Camera.renderingPath
description: Setting Camera.renderingPath has no effect under the Universal Render Pipeline, which selects its rendering path through the assigned Renderer on the URP Asset rather than the per-camera Built-in Render Pipeline property.
recommendation: Choose the rendering path by assigning the appropriate Renderer on the URP Asset instead of setting Camera.renderingPath.

title: Camera.depthTextureMode
description: Setting Camera.depthTextureMode does not drive depth texture generation under the Universal Render Pipeline, which produces _CameraDepthTexture based on the Depth Texture setting on the URP Asset. Code relying on this property may not get the depth it expects when migrating from the Built-in Render Pipeline.
recommendation: Enable Depth Texture on the URP Asset, or per-camera through UniversalAdditionalCameraData, instead of setting Camera.depthTextureMode.

title: Camera.depth
description: Setting Camera.depth controls how camera render outputs are ordered under the Built-in Render Pipeline. The Universal Render Pipeline composites multiple cameras through its Camera Stacking system (Base and Overlay cameras), so scripts relying on the Depth property for ordering may not produce the expected result when migrating from the Built-in Render Pipeline.
recommendation: Review whether this camera relies on Depth-based ordering and, if so, use URP Camera Stacking — designate a Base camera and add the others as Overlay cameras on its UniversalAdditionalCameraData stack — instead of setting Camera.depth.

title: ManagedDebugger usage
description: UnityEditor.Scripting.ManagedDebugger is part of the Mono scripting backend and is not supported under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime. Code that depends on it will not behave as expected after migrating to CoreCLR.
recommendation: Use System.Diagnostics.Debugger (for example, Debugger.IsAttached) instead of UnityEditor.Scripting.ManagedDebugger.

title: BinaryFormatter usage
description: BinaryFormatter is obsolete and is disabled under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, where its serialization and deserialization methods throw at runtime.
recommendation: Replace BinaryFormatter with a supported serializer such as JsonUtility, System.Text.Json, or DataContractSerializer, or write the data manually with BinaryReader and BinaryWriter.

title: Assembly.Location
description: Assembly.Location returns an empty string under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, because assemblies are no longer guaranteed to be loaded from a file on disk.
recommendation: Use Assembly.GetLoadedAssemblyPath() (an extension method in the UnityEngine namespace) to obtain an assembly's path instead of Assembly.Location.

title: Assembly.LoadFile
description: Assembly.LoadFile is not supported under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime and fails to load assemblies that the Editor or player has not already loaded.
recommendation: Load assemblies through CurrentAssemblies.LoadFromPath(string) or CurrentAssemblies.LoadFromBytes(byte[]) (in the UnityEngine.Assemblies namespace) instead of Assembly.LoadFile.

title: Assembly.LoadFrom
description: Assembly.LoadFrom is not supported under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime and fails to load assemblies that the Editor or player has not already loaded.
recommendation: Load assemblies through CurrentAssemblies.LoadFromPath(string) or CurrentAssemblies.LoadFromBytes(byte[]) (in the UnityEngine.Assemblies namespace) instead of Assembly.LoadFrom.

title: AppDomain.DomainUnload
description: Subscribing to AppDomain.DomainUnload no longer reliably fires under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, which does not unload the managed code space the way Mono does. Cleanup code that relies on this event may never run.
recommendation: Move cleanup that depends on AppDomain.DomainUnload to the [OnAssemblyUnloading] lifecycle attribute instead.

title: IntPtr.ToInt32
description: IntPtr.ToInt32 can throw OverflowException under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime when the pointer value does not fit in a 32-bit integer, which can happen on 64-bit platforms.
recommendation: Verify that this conversion cannot overflow. Prefer IntPtr.ToInt64() or keep the value as an IntPtr, or catch OverflowException where a narrowing conversion is required.

title: UIntPtr.ToUInt32
description: UIntPtr.ToUInt32 can throw OverflowException under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime when the pointer value does not fit in a 32-bit unsigned integer, which can happen on 64-bit platforms.
recommendation: Verify that this conversion cannot overflow. Prefer UIntPtr.ToUInt64() or keep the value as a UIntPtr, or catch OverflowException where a narrowing conversion is required.

title: Encoding.GetEncoding
description: Encoding.GetEncoding can throw NotSupportedException under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, which registers fewer code pages by default than the Mono scripting runtime did. Requesting an uncommon code page such as Windows-1252 fails unless its encoding provider has been registered.
recommendation: Prefer a built-in encoding such as Encoding.UTF8 where possible. If a code-page encoding is required, register the provider once at startup with Encoding.RegisterProvider(CodePagesEncodingProvider.Instance).

title: ArrayPool.Return
description: Returning a buffer to ArrayPool without clearing it leaves any object references stored in the array alive, which can keep those objects from being collected and interfere with code reloading under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime.
recommendation: Pass clearArray: true to ArrayPool.Return, or clear the buffer yourself before returning it, whenever the array holds references to managed objects.

title: System.Runtime.Remoting usage
description: System.Runtime.Remoting is part of .NET Framework remoting and is not available under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime. Code that uses it will fail to compile or run after migrating.
recommendation: Remove the dependency on System.Runtime.Remoting and replace it with a supported inter-process communication mechanism; there is no drop-in replacement package.

title: System.ServiceModel (WCF) usage
description: System.ServiceModel (Windows Communication Foundation) is not available under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime. Code that uses it will fail to compile or run after migrating.
recommendation: Remove the dependency on System.ServiceModel and replace it with a supported networking or RPC library; WCF has no drop-in replacement package.

title: System.Web usage
description: System.Web is part of ASP.NET on .NET Framework and is not available under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime. Code that uses it will fail to compile or run after migrating.
recommendation: Remove the dependency on System.Web and replace it with a supported alternative such as System.Net.Http or ASP.NET Core APIs; there is no drop-in replacement package.

title: System.Security.Permissions usage
description: System.Security.Permissions and Code Access Security are not supported under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, where these types are obsolete and have no effect.
recommendation: Remove Code Access Security calls; they cannot be replicated under CoreCLR. Rely on operating-system and process-level security instead.

title: System.Security.Policy usage
description: System.Security.Policy and Code Access Security are not supported under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, where these types are obsolete and have no effect.
recommendation: Remove Code Access Security policy code; it cannot be replicated under CoreCLR. Rely on operating-system and process-level security instead.

title: Microsoft.Win32.Registry usage
description: Microsoft.Win32.Registry is not part of the core libraries shipped with the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, so code that accesses the Windows registry through it will fail to resolve after migrating.
recommendation: Add the Microsoft.Win32.Registry NuGet package to keep using the registry APIs, and remember that the registry is only available on Windows.

title: System.Configuration usage
description: System.Configuration (the .NET Framework app.config and ConfigurationManager APIs) is not shipped with the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, so code that uses it will fail to resolve after migrating.
recommendation: Add the System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager NuGet package, or move configuration to a supported format such as JSON.

title: System.Drawing usage
description: System.Drawing is not shipped with the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, so code that uses it will fail to resolve after migrating.
recommendation: Add the System.Drawing.Common NuGet package (Windows only), or use Unity's own imaging APIs such as Texture2D instead.

title: AppDomain.CreateDomain
description: AppDomain.CreateDomain is not supported under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime, which cannot create additional application domains and throws when it is called.
recommendation: Remove use of additional AppDomain instances. Isolate code with separate processes or an AssemblyLoadContext instead.

title: Thread.Abort
description: Thread.Abort is not supported under the CoreCLR (.NET) scripting runtime and throws PlatformNotSupportedException when it is called.
recommendation: Use cooperative cancellation with a CancellationToken to stop background work instead of Thread.Abort.
